text: The Patriots secured a dominant 45-17 win over the Raiders on Sunday with Drake Maye accounting for five touchdowns in what appears to be a breakthrough performance, though the victory came at a significant cost to New England's roster health. Left tackle Will Campbell suffered an MCL sprain in his right knee and is expected to miss game action, while running back TreVeyon Henderson sustained a high ankle sprain that will sideline him for multiple weeks—a particularly brutal blow to a backfield that now turns to newly signed practice squad running back Hassan Haskins for depth. On a brighter note, the team bolstered its secondary by signing cornerback D'Shawn Jamison to the practice squad while releasing linebacker Jose Ramirez, and off the field, Patriots Hall of Famers Andre Tippett and Julian Edelman were announced as inductees into the International Jewish Sports Hall of Fame's Class of 2026. Despite missing his top receiver and both starting cornerbacks, Maye's impressive showing against Las Vegas suggests he may have found his confidence and deep ball timing after a rocky start to the season.
